explanation: This is safe. A fresh ArrayList is constructed on every call, so there is no shared mutable instance — each caller, sequential or concurrent, gets an independent list and can add or remove without corrupting anyone else's data. A tempting wrong answer assumes the method returns a shared static collection, but the local allocation prevents any cross-call aliasing.
prompt: Many callers invoke labels(). Can one caller's mutation corrupt another caller's result?
right_label: Shared instance — callers corrupt each other
